speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are presenting with sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down the leg; can you tell me how far down the pain travels and does it happen with specific movements? Also, do you have any numbness, weakness, or loss of bladder/bowel control?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Given the sudden onset during exercise and radiation into the foot, can you tell me if you noticed a distinct "pop" or tearing sensation, and do you have any visible bruising or swelling on your back or hip? REQUEST TEST: MRI Lumbar_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Lumbar_Spine: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Anemia cannot explain acute lower back pain radiating to the foot, so let's disregard that. Since you mentioned the pain worsens with movement, does coughing, sneezing, or straining cause a sudden increase in the pain or a "pop" sensation? REQUEST TEST: MRI Lumbar_Spine

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Lumbar_Spine: Evidence of L5-S1 disc herniation impinging on the adjacent nerve root.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: L5-S1 Disc Herniation. The MRI confirms the herniation is impinging on the nerve root, which explains your sharp pain radiating to your foot, and this finding supersedes the previous mention of anemia which does not fit your clinical presentation.
